claims.claim: Delivery work is I/O-bound (waiting on customer endpoints), so the number of deliveries in flight per Node.js process can be high (default 200)
claims.about: Node.js worker process (BullMQ worker, outbound HTTPS)
claims.measured: I/O-wait test at 256 connections, 10 ms waits: node-express 14,188 req/s at 92% CPU, node-fastify 17,462 req/s at 76% CPU
claims.why: One measured Node process handled 256 concurrent waiting requests easily, so keeping 200 slow requests open per process fits the data. The benchmark covers inbound requests, not outbound HTTPS, but the claim is about holding many waits open at once.

claims.claim: At the default of 200 deliveries in flight per process, peak load (~2,500 deliveries/s at ~1 s each) needs roughly 13 worker processes; average load needs one or two
claims.why: The number comes from dividing in-flight requests by the configured concurrency, not from runtime speed. The benchmarks measure inbound HTTP servers with 10 ms waits, not outbound HTTPS clients waiting 0.3–2 s, so they can't confirm how many processes are needed.
